formalDefinition: Unstructured Search = {(x, y) | x is int, y is int}
problemDefinition: Input: a function f:Σn→Σf:Σn→Σ; Output: a string x∈Σnx∈Σn satisfying f(x)=1,f(x)=1, or "no solution" if no such string xx exists
inputDescription: f, an oracle function given as its list of output bits
outputDescription: An index x such that f(x) = 1, or no solution if none exists
source: Grover, L. K. (1996). A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search. In Proceedings of the twenty-eighth annual ACM symposium on Theory of computing (pp. 212-219).
instanceFormat: Format: {y | y is list} (y = (f(0), f(1), ..., f(n-1)), the oracle function's output bits) Example: (0, 1, 0, 0)
certificateFormat: Format: i | integer index such that f(i) != 0, or 'no solution' when f(i) = 0 for every i Example: 1

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This solver simply loops through all possible x until one f(x) = 1.

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This verifier simply checks that the certificate provided results in f(x) != 0 for the unstructured search problem.
defaultVerifier.source: Grover, L. K. (1996). A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search. In Proceedings of the twenty-eighth annual ACM symposium on Theory of computing (pp. 212-219).

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This visualization builds a quantum circuit
defaultVisualization.source: Brassard, G., Hoyer, P., Mosca, M., & Tapp, A. (2000), Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation
